claims.text: As-cast or rapidly quenched HfNbTaTiZr is a disordered solid solution with minimal short-range chemical order and uniform baseline lattice parameters.
Annealing HfNbTaTiZr at 600–800 °C promotes short-range chemical order.
Rapid quenching maintains less short-range chemical order than annealing at 600–800 °C.
Short-range-ordered clusters generate heterogeneous local lattice distortions.
SRO-induced lattice distortions modify the alloy's intrinsic thermal-expansion mismatch.
Heterogeneous thermal expansion among local regions generates internal stress fields.
SRO-induced internal stress fields modify the elastic moduli of HfNbTaTiZr at intermediate temperatures.
SRO-induced internal stress fields enhance the high-temperature creep resistance of HfNbTaTiZr.
SRO-induced lattice distortions cause the hardening observed after aging.
Relative to rapidly quenched material, annealed HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit diffuse scattering or weak superlattice peaks attributable to SRO.
Relative to rapidly quenched material, annealed HfNbTaTiZr will have increased elastic moduli over 293–1100 K.
Relative to rapidly quenched material, annealed HfNbTaTiZr will have a lower creep rate and therefore improved creep resistance at approximately 1250 °C.
High-resolution imaging or atom-probe tomography will quantitatively reveal the presence and spacing of SRO clusters.
The proposed SRO effect will occur from 293 K to 1250 °C and will be strongest in the 600–800 °C aging regime and near the 1250 °C creep condition.
